newsitem.title: USA: US late spot prods, led by heat, slip with futures.
newsitem.headline: US late spot prods, led by heat, slip with futures.

text.p: U.S. cash refined products, led by heating oil, stumbled with NYMEX futures late Monday amid narrowly mixed differentials, players said.
But deals were few and far between as traders from around the country flocked to the annual National Petroleum Refiners Association conference in San Antonio, Texas. The event lasts through Tuesday.
"People will start getting back to work Tuesday and Wednesday but right now the market is asleep," one Gulf player said, calling Monday one of the slowest trading days of the year.

NYH heating oil was offered at about 0.15 cents over April futures, a bit firmer than Friday diffs, while prompt Gulf heat eased about 0.30 cent to 2.25 cents below the screen. April futures, meanwhile, settled 1.03 cents lower to 54.30 cents a gallon.

New York Harbor conventional unleaded "M4" gasoline was offered at 3.85 cents below April futures in thin talk, stable with Friday differentials, while Gulf Coast back ninth cycle "M3" unleaded was also steady at about 3.75 cents under, traders said.
((- Ransdell Pierson, New York Energy Desk, 212 859-1632))
